$comment: THE 2023 LANGUAGE ELEMENT STANDINGS, held once as data (kb/Work PB4993; DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md section
10.2): the archaic language elements of §2023:F.1, which §2023:4.2.12 defines, and the obsolete language elements of
§2023:F.2, which §2023:4.2.13 defines. The shape is the 1985 file's (spec-element-standing-1985.json, whose comment
states each key): per list its `standing`, its locator, its `remarks` and its entries; per entry its number, its
`terms`, its `sections`, optional `section-terms` and optional `section-formats` (a SHARED section's numbered formats
that are wholly the element: every syntax and general rule of their band is marked). A section is the element's
SPECIFICATION; OWN or SHARED is derived from its heading (element_standing.own). EXIT PROGRAM is Format 2 (program) of
the EXIT statement. The VALIDATE facility owns the clauses that exist only for it (CLASS, DEFAULT, DESTINATION,
INVALID, VALIDATE-STATUS; the validation-clauses of §2023:13.16.2) and shares the data description entry (its Format 4
(validation)), the PRESENT WHEN clause (Format 2 (validation)), the VALUE clause (Format 5 (content-validation-entry),
and its VALID and INVALID phrases), the VARYING clause (it serves report writer too) and the exception-name table.
standing sentence is not an element's specification: a definition's note, Annex A's processor-dependent and optional
element lists, and Annex D's informative concepts. extract_rule_catalog.py applies the lists (each rule's `status`)

remarks.why: the definition of a term, whose note names the element's standing
